description: Protecting Fish to Save Coral Reefs is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA Fisheries | Pacific Islands Fisheries Science Center | Coral Reef Ecosystem Program; State of Hawaiʻi | Division of Aquatic Resources; University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa | Department of Botany. Coral reefs off the west coast of Maui are readily accessible and heavily used by visitors and locals alike. Managers needed a plan to boost the resilience of the reefs so they could continue providing critical habitat for marine species. Coverage: the United States (2016). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
